Subject: DPA details + AI training/no-training commitments

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and security teams have a few follow-ups before we can finalize procurement:

- We need an explicit contractual commitment that Acme Health data (including prompts and model outputs) will not be used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any public or private models unless we provide express written opt-in.
- Confirmation that prompts and model responses are treated as customer data and that Acme retains ownership.
- A current list of subprocessors (and a process for prior notice / objection).
- Mechanism for EU / cross-border transfers (SCCs, adequacy, or equivalent).
- Any standard audit/evidence you can share (SOC2 + sample logs).

Subject: Re: DPA details + AI training/no-training commitments

Hi Helen — thanks for the clear list. I attached a redline of our standard DPA with suggested language that addresses each bullet (redline_DPA_20260301.pdf). High level answers here: 

- No-training: Redwood provides an explicit no-training commitment option. For Dedicated and Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) we do not use customer data to improve shared models by default. For Hosted API customers, we offer two paths: (1) retain default telemetry for service improvement (opt-in), or (2) contractually-disabled model-improvement where we implement a do-not-train flag and exclude your data from internal training pipelines. The proposed contract language in section 4.2 covers this and an operational implementation note (flagging + retention isolation).

- Ownership: Our standard position is that customers retain rights to prompts and outputs. We propose simple IP language confirming customer ownership of prompt/response content and a limited license to Redwood solely for providing the service and for security/operations (no model training).

- Subprocessors: We maintain a published subprocessors page. We also include a 30-day notice period for material changes and a short objection window in the DPA. Link to subprocessors list provided in the redline.

- EU transfers: Redwood executes the EU Standard Contractual Clauses for controller-processor transfers and can add the EU Data Processing Addendum. For Dedicated/Private in-region deployments, data can remain in-region per your requirement.

- Audit evidence: We can share SOC 2 Type II and a sample latency/cost breakdown for the routes relevant to your traffic. Operational logs are available under a governance package; we propose a sample export with redaction.

I've copied Sean and Kimberly so we can align commercial and legal asks. Would you like a 30-minute call this week to walk through the redline?

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel

Subject: Internal: Acme DPA alignment (no-training clause & audit)

Team — internal alignment notes before the call: 

- Customer asks: explicit no-training for all customer data unless they opt-in, prompt/response ownership, subprocessors transparency, SCCs for cross-border, sample logs.
- Proposed Redwood approach (already in redline):
  * Contractual "No-Training Commitment" (Section 4.2): for Hosted API, operationalized via a customer opt-out flag; for Dedicated/Private, default no-training.
  * IP language: Customer retains all rights to prompts/responses; Redwood gets a narrow license to operate the service and for security/ops only.
  * Subprocessors: public list + 30-day notice + objection mechanism; major infra changes require escalation to legal.
  * EU transfers: SCCs + in-region hosting options.
  * Audit: provide SOC2 summary + sample logs (redacted) under NDA.

Open points for negotiation: retention period for logs (customer asked for 12 months; propose 90 days default, 12 months on request under governance addendum), and whether they require periodic independent audits vs. SOC2 bridge reports.

Kimberly — can you confirm whether a 90-day default log retention with ability to extend to 12 months under a governance addendum is acceptable? Also, any redline suggestions for an explicit "do-not-train" operational SLA (we should define required lead time and verification steps).

Sean — on the call please surface whether Acme intends to route prod traffic via Hosted API or Dedicated — affects timeline and our ability to promise default no-training.

Thanks,
Monica

Subject: Final redline & next steps — DPA + DocuSign

Hi Helen — thanks for the productive conversation earlier. Attached is a tidy redline (acme_dpa_redline_20260303.docx) that incorporates the no-training commitment, explicit IP/ownership language, subprocessors notice period, and SCCs language. Summary below: 

- No-Training: Redwood will not use Acme Health data (prompts, responses, or derived artifacts) to train or improve models unless Acme provides prior written consent. Operationally, we will (a) set a tenant-level do-not-train flag on your account upon execution of the DPA, and (b) exclude flagged data from any internal training or telemetry pipelines.
- Ownership: Acme retains ownership of prompts and responses. Redwood receives a limited license to process data to provide the service, for security, and to comply with law.
- Subprocessors: We listed current subprocessors and commit to 30 days' notice on material changes; you have an objection process (details in section 7).
- EU Transfers: We will execute SCCs and can host data in EU regions if you choose Dedicated/Private deployment.
- Audit/Logs: We will supply SOC2 Type II and an operational log export (redacted). Default log retention: 90 days. Extension to 12 months available by governance addendum.

If the redline looks OK, I've initiated a DocuSign envelope for the DPA and governance addendum: https://docusign.com/AcmeHealth-Redwood-DPA-DEAL-4721. Once signed we will set the do-not-train flag and confirm operational controls within one business day.

Please let me know if you want any further edits. Happy to loop in our infra team for a short architectural note on Dedicated in-region hosting if useful.

Best regards,
Monica Patel
